Why taxpayers cover the bill in cases like this
Federal civil rights lawsuits, like the one in this story, run on a federal law known as Section 1983, which lets people sue government officials, including police officers, who violate their constitutional rights.
However, there is a Qualified Immunity that shields government officials from being sued individually for money damages in civil court — and if a judge grants an officer Qualified Immunity early in a lawsuit, the case against that specific officer is completely dismissed.
This may not be the case for the Utah officers in this story.
American Fork Police Chief Cameron Paul publicly admitted the department made errors regarding the warrant affidavit, saying "we didn't do this perfectly" and "several issues weren't handled well, or were handled outside of policy," ABC4.com reported.
Because the chief admitted to procedural errors and officers were recorded admitting intent to scare citizens, the city faces significant legal exposure.
If the court finds the officers acted with reckless disregard for constitutional rights, Qualified Immunity may be stripped.
However, even if an officer loses Qualified Immunity, goes to trial and loses the civil lawsuit, they still rarely pay a dime. This is due to a process called indemnification.
Ultimately, the money used to pay the victims of police misconduct comes out of the city's budget or insurance policies funded by taxpayers, not the individual officer's bank account.
What the Mansell family has recovered so far
According to a Central Oregon Daily article, on Aug. 19, Bricks & Minifigs announced a "comprehensive and amicable resolution of a private civil dispute" with the Mansell family, compensating them with an undisclosed amount and issuing an "unqualified apology."
It stressed the deal was "a compromise of disputed claims, not an admission of liability or wrongdoing."
Bryan Mansell releases all claims against Bricks & Minifigs, which in turn drops its suit against him — but the lawsuits against Reckless Ben still remain active.
A GoFundMe set up by Schneider for Mansell has raised $531,411 of a $550,000 target at the time of writing.

Investors often weigh stable, brick-and-mortar retailers against high-growth digital platforms. Choosing between Advance Auto Parts (AAP +1.03%) and Airbnb (ABNB +0.84%) depends on whether you prioritize value or growth in your portfolio.
Advance Auto Parts focuses on the essential automotive repair market through a vast physical network. Airbnb operates a capital-light digital platform that revolutionized the hospitality industry. While they belong to the same consumer discretionary sector, their business models offer very different paths for long-term investors.
Advance Auto Parts operates as a major provider in the automotive aftermarket, selling parts and accessories to a diverse customer base. The company splits its business between professional installers and do-it-yourself (DIY) customers, with professional sales accounting for approximately 50% of revenue in 2025. It remains a fixture among retail stocks by operating 4,311 stores and supporting nearly 800 independently owned Carquest locations. In January 2026, the company expanded its private-label offerings by launching Argos, a brand designed to capture value-conscious shoppers.
Financial performance has faced headwinds recently as the company navigates a changing retail landscape. According to its latest annual report filed for FY 2025, revenue reached about $8.6 billion, representing a decrease of approximately 5.4% compared to the prior year. Despite the dip in sales, the company reported net income of roughly $44 million for the period. This resulted in a net margin, which measures the percentage of revenue kept as profit, of approximately 0.5%.
As of its January 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was roughly 2.4x. This ratio measures financial leverage by comparing total debt to shareholder equity. Its current ratio, which indicates how easily a company can pay its short-term bills using its assets, stood at approximately 1.7x. Free cash flow for the fiscal year was negative, at minus-$298.0 million. Free cash flow equals cash flow from operations minus capital expenditures and represents the cash a business generates after accounting for investments in its physical assets.
Airbnb manages a global marketplace that connects hosts with travelers seeking unique stays and experiences. The company does not own the properties listed; instead, it provides the digital infrastructure for more than 5 million hosts to list their homes. This capital-light model allows the platform to scale rapidly across 220 countries and regions. By focusing on a two-sided network, the company benefits from a self-sustaining cycle where more hosts attract more guests, and vice versa.
Growth remains a central theme for the travel leader as it expands its international footprint. In FY 2025, revenue reached about $12.3 billion, which indicates a growth rate of approximately 10.3% over the previous year. The company reported net income of roughly $2.5 billion for the same period. This led to a net margin of approximately 20.4%, showing that the company retains a significant portion of its sales as profit after all expenses are paid.
As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was approximately 0.3x. This indicates a conservative level of debt relative to equity. Its current ratio was roughly 1.4x, suggesting the company maintains sufficient liquidity to meet its near-term obligations. Free cash flow reached nearly $4.6 billion in FY 2025. Note that stock-based compensation (SBC) represented roughly 34% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.
Advance Auto Parts faces significant competitive threats from national automotive retailers like AutoZone Inc. (AZO +2.01%) and O'Reilly Automotive Inc. (ORLY +1.07%), as well as mass merchandisers like Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN +0.07%). The company is currently exposed to operational risks from its ongoing restructuring efforts, including potential costs from lease terminations and store closures. Furthermore, cybersecurity remains a concern following a previous data breach settlement, while global logistics disruptions and trade tariffs could impact its supply chain stability.
Airbnb is subject to high competitive pressure in the travel industry from search engines and hotel chains, as well as online travel agencies like Booking Holdings Inc. (BKNG +0.81%). The platform faces ongoing regulatory risks as various local and international governments implement short-term rental bans or restrictions. Additionally, the company is exposed to financial risks from its dependence on cloud hosting infrastructure and ongoing legal disputes with tax authorities regarding the valuation of its intellectual property.
Airbnb carries a much higher valuation reflecting its double-digit growth, while Advance Auto Parts trades at a deep discount amid its business turnaround.

Which stock would I buy in 2026?
Advance Auto Parts is in the midst of turning around the struggles it has experienced over the past few years around sales growth, margins, and market share. The aftermarket auto parts business has been in a slump, due largely to a mix of factors: weak do-it-yourselfer demand, vehicle electrification, intense competition, and general pocketbook pressures on consumers.
Company management has been addressing the business' issues by rolling out a new multi-year turnaround program. That started in late 2024, including closing stores, optimizing store footprints, and overhauling its supply chain. To date, the program has produced mixed results. First-quarter fiscal 2026 results that were much better than expected, with revenue of $2.6 billion and net income of $25 million. But the second quarter disappointed the street, and shares plunged as revenue fell short of consensus at $2 billion, even as net income and other metrics beat expectations.
Analysts see full-year 2026 sales a little lower at $8.57 billion, with net income improving to $167 million, roughly four times 2025.
Airbnb reported an excellent second quarter of fiscal 2026, rallying shares sharply after results. The business beat consensus revenue estimates by $100 million, reporting $3.6 billion in sales, up 17% from the same period in 2025, driven by a strong increase in booked nights. Foreign markets like India and Latin America, two markets in which Airbnb is seeking growth, were exceptionally strong. The third quarter should see sales close to $4.8 billion and net income around $1.7 billion.
The business is finding ways to expand its popular travel business, embracing features like buy now, pay later (BNPL) on reservations, a form of short-term lending. The network advantage of Airbnb's history, over 2 billion guest arrivals since 2008, and the lack of host presence on AI (meaning a competitor using AI has little data and information to scrape in order to form a competing product) give it a competitive moat.
For the full year, management expects sales of $14.1 billion with net income of $3.2 billion.
So which stock to choose? In the highly competitive retail sector, Advance Auto Parts is by no means guaranteed success despite its strong efforts to recover. Airbnb's capital-light model also means it has far fewer competitive moats. But it's the healthier and faster-growing business of the two, and until the company can't execute and competitors catch up, it appears to be a long-term buy.

Airbnb (ABNB) put its fall product update front and center this week, spotlighting AI-powered search and new on-trip services that tighten the link between its travel platform and day-to-day trip logistics.
Recent price action has been broadly supportive of that story, with a 30.59% year to date share price return and a 37.96% total shareholder return over the past year, suggesting that momentum has been building as Airbnb rolls out product upgrades and investors reassess its risk and growth profile.

Airbnb now trades close to analyst targets, yet internal fair value estimates still suggest a sizable gap. Is this latest AI-fueled rally already pricing in the story, or is that 40% implied discount too wide?
Most Popular Narrative: 4.5% Undervalued
Airbnb's most followed valuation storyline pegs fair value at $181.84 per share compared with the recent $173.70 close. This points to a modest upside gap that still needs to be justified by the underlying business mix and product momentum.
"This is the first time in a while where Airbnb is not asking investors to believe that the next growth engine is coming. Some of it is actually showing up. Core markets are accelerating again. International markets are still growing quickly. AI is reducing costs. The core product is converting better. Hotels are gaining traction. Experiences are at least moving in the right direction. And profitability remains very strong."

According to TickerTickle, that fair value view rests on a few key levers. The narrative uses a 12% annual revenue growth rate, a 24.5% long term net margin and a future P/E of 27x, all discounted at 8.5%. Those inputs combine into a fair value estimate of $181.84, only slightly above the current share price yet still meaningfully below the $290.97 future cash flow value implied by the SWS DCF model.
This creates an interesting split for readers. The DCF output and Simply Wall St valuation checks flag Airbnb as trading 40.3% below future cash flow value. The popular narrative frames the gap as a 4.5% discount to fair value. That tension often reflects different expectations for how quickly earnings and free cash flow convert into shareholder returns, rather than a disagreement about the direction of the business itself.
For now, the story that markets seem to be responding to is clear. Airbnb has become profitable, is generating high quality earnings, carries a high 34.5% forecast return on equity in three years and has been using strong free cash flow to fund buybacks and reduce share count. At the same time, earnings are projected to grow 15.55% per year, which is slightly slower than the broader US market, so investors still need to decide how much to pay for that mix of quality and growth.

Airbnb recently rolled out a fall product update that connects travelers with friends' trips, introduces AI-powered search, and adds on-trip services like Instacart grocery delivery, laundry, baby gear rentals, and local experiences.
The tighter integration of AI search with services such as grocery and gear delivery points to Airbnb pushing deeper into higher-fee, non-lodging spend across each trip.
We will now look at how Airbnb's investment narrative is shaped by these AI-powered search upgrades and expanded on-trip services.

To own Airbnb, you have to believe it can keep turning a global host network, strong direct traffic, and an expanding services layer into consistent earnings while staying ahead of new AI booking agents and regulation. The fall product update sits right on that thesis. It tightens the link between discovery, booking, and on-trip spend, but does not change the core near term driver, which is execution on the broader travel platform vision.
The biggest short term swing factor is how effectively Airbnb can grow higher fee experiences, hotels, and services without eroding guest or host satisfaction. The main risk remains external pressure, from AI intermediaries that could sit between Airbnb and users, and from city level rules that may limit supply. The new features are helpful but not decisive against either issue yet.
The most relevant piece of the recent rollout is the AI powered search that lets you describe a trip in natural language and see homes, experiences, and services in one view. For investors, this speaks directly to two things that matter for Airbnb: how efficiently the marketplace matches supply and demand, and how much of a trip's wallet the platform can realistically capture.
Execution is what counts. If AI summaries and side by side comparisons reduce search friction, guests may be more willing to book longer stays, try hotels on Airbnb, or attach services like grocery delivery and laundry. That supports the existing catalyst around experiences and services raising revenue per booking, but it also raises the bar on product quality. Any mismatch between AI recommendations, actual listings, and on trip services would quickly show up in reviews and support costs.
Airbnb's narrative projects US$18.6b revenue and US$4.7b earnings by 2029. That path assumes revenue growing at 12.3% per year and an earnings increase of about US$2b from US$2.7b today.

Airbnb's Brian Chesky barely writes one email a week — while Uber's CEO expects weekend replies
Fri, October 16, 2026 at 4:00 PM CDT 5 min read
Brian Chesky, 45, the CEO of San Francisco-based home-sharing company Airbnb, [NASDAQ:ABNB] has pretty much given up on writing emails. He still answers the ones that land in his inbox, but when he needs something from his team, he picks up his phone and texts them instead.
"I don't know if I write an email a week," Chesky said in an interview with Time. Texts are a different story, he explained, because, "When you get a text message, it doesn't feel like work to respond."

Among big-company CEOs who've talked publicly about how they communicate, he's in the minority. Nvidia's Jensen Huang and Uber's Dara Khosrowshahi, for example, still do a lot of their managing over email.
Most office workers couldn't skip email if they tried, since Microsoft 365 users get 117 emails a day on average and give most of them less than a minute, according to a report published June by Microsoft.
Chesky told Time that if he had to rank how he likes to communicate, face-to-face conversations would come first, then Zoom, then texting, with email likely in last place. Emails start with a subject line, he pointed out, whereas a text goes straight to someone.
When something needs fixing, he'd rather sit down with the person, call them or fire off a text than open his inbox.

Which CEOs still run their companies by email?
Then there's Huang, 63, CEO of chipmaker Nvidia [NASDAQ:NVDA], who works almost the opposite way. Nvidia staff have long emailed him short notes known inside the company as "Top-5 Things" — each a rundown of what they're working on and noticing. He goes through those notes daily to catch early hints of where the business is heading, The Wall Street Journal reported in December, 2024.
Over at ride-hailing company Uber [NYSE:UBER], CEO Dara Khosrowshahi, 57, wants his staff to answer emails on weekends. On a Feb. 23 episode of The Diary of a CEO, he said anyone who doesn't answer his Saturday email can expect a pointed follow-up from him on Sunday.
Late-night work is creeping up for everyone else, too. The number of meetings kicking off after 8 p.m. rose 16% in a year, according to Microsoft's report, and a typical employee now trades more than 50 messages outside the 9-to-5.
In Microsoft's 2025 Work Trend Index survey of 31,000 knowledge workers across 31 markets, 48% of employees and 52% of leaders said their work feels "chaotic and fragmented."
How to reach a boss who barely uses email
You can simply ask your manager (maybe during your next one-on-one) where they prefer to read work messages, whether that's email, Slack, Teams, or even texts.
And for anything important, it helps to cover your bases. Any serious communication should be in writing. That would include things like a raise request, a change in your duties, or a deadline you want on record. But there's no harm in sending a quick text to let your boss know it's there. And if you need an answer within the hour, a call or a text is probably your best bet, since that's how Chesky deals with his own urgent problems.
It also pays to find out what your boss expects after hours, because being reachable all the time can wear you down. In a June 2026 analysis, Eurofound, the Dublin-based EU agency that studies working conditions, found that stress at work climbs with how often people are contacted outside their hours. Among workers across the European Union who get contacted every day after hours, 59% say they feel stress at work always or almost always. That falls to 17% among those who are never contacted. The figures come from the agency's 2024 European Working Conditions Survey.
Interestingly enough, managers are more likely than any other group of workers to get those after-hours messages, according to Eurofound.
Chesky, for his part, says he tries not to text people he believes are spending time with family, emergencies aside. If your boss has never said whether they follow a similar rule, it's a fair question to bring up.

What Changed In Airbnb's Story?
Tue, October 20, 2026 at 3:23 PM CDT 3 min read
Airbnb (ABNB) stock trades at 38.6 times earnings, against 22.9 for the S&P 500. Shareholders paying that much need to know what they are buying, but there is a twist: what management talks up on its calls has changed. During the fiscal Q3 2024 call, management said it was focused on making hosting just as popular as traveling on Airbnb, which means getting more people to rent out their homes. On the latest call, management made the case for something else. So what is it?
During the fiscal Q2 2026 call in August, management highlighted hotels, saying hotel nights are growing about three times faster than the homes business. The company also described the next stage for Airbnb as a one-stop shop for travel, and said it had expanded Airbnb Services into grocery delivery, car rental, airport pickup and luggage storage.
Before that, hosts were the supply story. Management introduced co-host networks on the fiscal Q3 2024 call as an easy way for a homeowner to find a local host to run the listing. By the fiscal Q2 2025 call, management said 100,000 listings were managed by co-hosts and that the program could lead to millions more homes on Airbnb. Co-hosts did not come up on the latest call, and hotels took the spotlight. Homes still got attention: management said more than 150,000 homes in World Cup host cities were listed on Airbnb for the first time.
How Big Are Hotels Next To Airbnb's Homes?
Hotels still represent a small part of Airbnb. Management said on the fiscal Q2 2026 call that they account for a single-digit percentage of nights booked. As a result, homes still make up the great bulk of what guests book, even with hotel nights growing about three times as fast.
Management said nights and seats booked grew 10% from a year earlier, accelerating from fiscal Q1 2026. Revenue grew 16.5% in fiscal Q2 2026, faster than the 12.7% growth in fiscal Q2 2025.
Should Airbnb Holders Worry About Its Push Into Hotels?
So far the push reads as more reassuring than concerning, because Airbnb as a whole is growing faster, not slower. Revenue over the twelve months to June 2026 grew 13.6%, against 10.2% for the twelve months before. the most relevant promotions and credits for each guest, as well as eligible payment options. ¦ Interest-free installments: Eligible guests in Mexico and Brazil can now pay with interest- free installments. For hosts Pricing - Effective pricing
is one of the biggest drivers of host success. We introduced simpler pricing and more flexible cancellation policies to help hosts succeed. ¦ Simplified pricing in Airbnb Setup: New hosts can more easily set die ff rent weekday and weekend
rates. ¦ Single service fee for API hosts: Hosts can more easily set the same price guests see. ¦ Updated cancellation policies: We migrated eligible listings from Strict to Firm cancellation policies, helping hosts attract more bookings.
Recommendations and insights - We’re providing hosts with more personalized recommendations and insights to help them improve their listings, attract more bookings, and increase their earning potential. ¦ Personalized recommendations:
Tailored suggestions help hosts improve their listings, calendar availability, and pricing, with proactive notifications that can help them take action. ¦ Quality insights: Hosts receive specic s fi uggestions for improvement based on recent
guest reviews. Host tools and onboarding - We removed friction throughout the hosting journey, making it easier for hosts to get started, manage their listings, and grow their business. ¦ Updated earnings dashboard: Hosts can now track their
year-over-year performance and better understand earnings trends. ¦ Improved listing editor: Hosts can more easily highlight important details about their home, including sleeping arrangements. 4
Expanding what Airbnb oe ff rs In addition to making Airbnb better for
hosts and guests, we’re continuing to expand what Airbnb offers. Our 2026 Summer Release marked the next step in that journey. ¦ Airbnb Services: We expanded Airbnb Services to include grocery delivery, car rentals, airport pickups, and
luggage storage. These services address some of the biggest pain points guests face while traveling. And we recently introduced resort passes, giving guests day access to amenities at some of the world’s best hotels. It’s still early
days, but we’re seeing real momentum—both in guests’ bookings and how quickly we’re scaling these partner services. ¦ Airbnb Experiences: We added thousands of new Experiences across our most in-demand categories,
increasing Airbnb Experiences supply by nearly 80% year-over-year in Q2 2026. As our selection grew, demand grew alongside it, with seats booked accelerating year-over- year and quarter-over-quarter. ¦ Boutique and independent hotels: We added
thousands of boutique and independent hotels to Airbnb across more than 20 top destinations, including New York, Paris, London, Madrid, Rome, and Singapore, with more markets coming this year. Featured hotels come with a price 1 match guarantee and
up to 15% Airbnb credit that guests can use toward their next booking. 2 Approximately 35% of first time guests who book a hotel on Airbnb return to book a home. While hotels still represent a single-digit percentage of nights booked, they’re
seeing signic fi ant growth. In fact, hotel nights booked grew approximately three times as fast as our homes business. Building AI into every part of the trip As part of our 2026 Summer Release, we introduced AI tools that make Airbnb easier to use
at every stage of the trip. For guests, our AI models can now generate highlights from host listing descriptions and guest reviews, making it easier to quickly find information about the things they care about most, like location, amenities, or
whether a home is family friendly. Later this year, we’ll introduce AI-generated home comparisons that help guests compare homes across the key attributes that matter most to them. For hosts, we’re rolling out AI-assisted tools that make
it easier for them to create a listing and understand pricing and earning opportunities. AI is also transforming customer support. Our AI assistant, now available in more than 50 languages, has 3 been rated the best AI support assistant in travel.
Nearly 45% of issues that begin with our AI assistant are now resolved without a human agent, up from Q1, while delivering much faster resolution times. Later this year, we’ll begin introducing an AI voice assistant, extending that experience
to phone calls. 1 Applicable only for select hotels. Price match requests must be made within 24 hours of booking. Max credit of $400 USD or local currency equivalent. Price difference is calculated excluding fees and taxes. Credit valid for 1 year.
Terms and exclusions apply. In addition, the 15% credit offer is valid until 12/31/2026 on eligible hotels. Credit calculation excludes fees and taxes. Credit valid for 1 year. Max credit of $2,000 USD or local currency equivalent. Terms and
exclusions apply. 2 Based on guests who booked a hotel on Airbnb between July 2024 and June 2025 and came back to book a home on Airbnb within the following 365 days. 3 Based on benchmarking conducted by a leading third-party consulting firm between
March and April 2026 comparing AI customer support assistants across six major travel platforms in the US. Evaluation assessed performance across support quality, issue resolution, task completion, and overall conversational experience. 5
These improvements are also making our business more efficient. In Q2,
our customer support related cost per booking declined approximately 16% year-over-year, driven in part by improvements to our AI assistant. We expect this cost to continue declining as our AI assistant resolves a broader range of issues and we
introduce new capabilities. Major events as a growth engine Major events help us strengthen the Airbnb brand while growing both supply and demand. By partnering with organizers around the world, we introduce millions of people to Airbnb, encourage
more people to become hosts, and help cities welcome more visitors. The brand awareness and trust these partnerships create can benefit our business long after the event ends. The FIFA World Cup 2026™ is one recent example of this strategy in
action. As an official Tournament Supporter, Airbnb hosted millions of guest arrivals during the tournament, including many first-time users. More than 150,000 homes across host cities were listed on Airbnb for the first time, helping provide an
economic uplift for the local community. Beyond the World Cup, we’re building a repeatable playbook that scales across global, regional, and local events. Partners include the International Olympic Committee, Tour de France, Art Basel fairs,
Lollapalooza festivals, La Liga in Spain, and most recently NASCAR. As we expand these partnerships, we’ll continue strengthening the Airbnb brand and supporting travel demand in destinations around the world. 6
Outlook We’re pleased with the results we’ve delivered in
the first half of 2026, and are excited about the continued traction from our product innovation and strong demand on our platform across all regions that is driving momentum in the second half of 2026. Given this strength, we are raising our
full-year outlook for both revenue growth and Adjusted EBITDA Margin. The uplift in revenue growth and margin reflects the strong demand on our platform, benefits from investments we’ve made in talent, technology, and marketing as well as
strong execution across our product roadmap. We continue to focus on investing behind our growth initiatives. Q3 2026 ¦ We expect to generate revenue of $4.69 billion to $4.77 billion, representing year-over-year growth of 15% to 17%, inclusive
of an approximate three percentage point FX tailwind after factoring in our hedging program. We expect our implied take rate to remain relatively in-line year-over-year. ¦ We expect year-over-year GBV growth to be in the mid teens, driven by
low double-digit growth in Nights and Seats Booked and a moderate increase in ADR due to mix shift and price appreciation. ¦ We expect Adjusted EBITDA to increase year-over-year and Adjusted EBITDA Margin to be down slightly compared to Q3
2025, due to timing of investments. Full-year 2026 ¦ For full-year 2026, we now expect year-over-year revenue growth to improve to at least mid teens, supported by the accelerated pace of Nights and Seats Booked we’ve observed, traction
from product and growth initiatives, as well as continued strong travel demand. ¦ For 2026, we now expect to deliver a full-year Adjusted EBITDA Margin of at least 35.5%— an improvement from 2025 that reflects stronger topline growth and
underlying operating leverage in our core business, while continuing to invest behind opportunities to drive future growth. 7
A CLOSER LOOK Helpful services at your service Great trips include more
than where you stay. Travel is easier when there’s a rental car ready to go, a place to store luggage before check-in, or groceries delivered to your door. These new services are the first of many ways we’re making the whole trip
GUEST SPOTLIGHT Driving guest growth To boost guest conversion, we
redesigned the homepage, streamlined the sign-up flow, and introduced more flexible cancellation and expanded payment options. Search and discovery Login and sign-up The personalized homepage helps guests find the perfect home, An entirely new login
and sign-up flow has improved how easily experience, or service for their trip. new and returning guests access Airbnb. Flexible cancellation policies Payments and checkout Guests book with more confidence now that it’s easier The flexibility
of Reserve Now, Pay Later and a streamlined checkout to understand their cancellation options before booking. experience makes it easier for guests to complete their booking. 9
HOST SPOTLIGHT More host bookings We added more personalized insights
across the app to help hosts attract bookings, and new tools to better manage and promote their listings. Recommendations and insights Tailored suggestions are built into the app to help hosts improve their listings, attract more bookings, and
increase their earnings. Ee ff ctive pricing Improved earnings dashboard We simplified Airbnb Setup to make it easier for new hosts The new, more insightful dashboard helps hosts track their year- to fine-tune their weekday and weekend pricing.
over-year performance and better understand earnings trends. 10
Business and Financial Performance Q2 2026 148.3M $27.2B Nights and
Seats Booked Gross Booking Value 10% Y/Y 16% Y/Y 15% Y/Y (ex-FX) In Q2 2026, Nights and Seats Booked grew 10% year-over-year, representing an acceleration relative to Q1 2026, primarily driven by strong demand across all regions and continued
momentum behind our product roadmap including search and merchandising, pricing and tools, and flexible payments. Additionally, growth continued to be driven in part by our app strategy, with nights booked on our app in Q2 2026 increasing 23%
year-over-year and accounting for 64% of total nights booked—up from 59% in the prior-year period. In addition, we saw year-over-year growth of first-time bookers accelerate to 11% in Q2 2026—the highest in four years—with
continued strong growth in Brazil, Japan, and India. In Q2 2026, GBV was $27.2 billion, representing a year-over-year increase of 16%. On an ex-FX basis, GBV increased 15% year-over-year—two percentage points higher than Q1 2026—driven
by improving growth of Nights and Seats Booked, as well as an increase in ADR. ADR was $184 in Q2 2026, increasing 5% compared to Q2 2025. On an ex-FX basis, ADR in Q2 2026 increased 4% year-over-year and was up across all regions—
particularly North America and EMEA—due to price appreciation and mix. Specifically, in Q2 2026, we saw entire homes, especially listings with four or more bedrooms continue to grow the fastest. Bedroom Nights Booked Group travel remains one
